exposure: offspring being small for gestational age (SGA)
cohort: The study included liveborn, singleton births in Denmark between 1997 and 2019 (n = 1,113,708) and Norway between 2008 and 2018 (n = 470,270).
finding: Each perinatal exposure individually increased the risk of hospitalised childhood infection, with a cumulative risk observed for an increasing number of exposures, particularly among preterm children with additional exposures.
mod_finding: Caesarean section birth was individually associated with a greater risk of hospitalised infection, although a specific hazard ratio for it alone was not detailed beyond being one of the seven exposures contributing to cumulative risk.
